title: Optimal limits on weak integrability breaking and protected thermal memory near qutrit exchange
abstract: Although integrability does not universally require a continuous one-site symmetry, we rigorously prove that every jointly analytic, regular Yang-Baxter deformation of the qutrit exchange interaction necessarily retains a nontrivial, analytically varying one-site charge. Breaking this local symmetry imposes a fundamental physical constraint on approximate conservation, governed by the optimal uniform bound $δ^3 \le C\varepsilon$ that explicitly relates the minimal one-site symmetry defect $δ$ to the local current-conservation residual $\varepsilon$. While breaking all one-site charges strictly forbids an exact integrable completion, an optimally compensated nearest-neighbor interaction saturates this cubic limit and anomalously extends the guaranteed infinite-temperature energy-current correlation window to order $|λ|^{-3}$ in the perturbation strength $λ$. Furthermore, we reveal a fundamental resonance obstruction for intrinsic conversion perturbations that strictly prevents any exact first-order repair of a broken one-site charge on any finite ring. Nevertheless, we demonstrate that the complete eight-dimensional charge memory matrix remains thermodynamically protected and approaches the identity for timescales $t=o(|λ|^{-3/2})$, a robust feature of the full infinite-temperature dynamics when the thermodynamic limit is taken before weak coupling.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the optimal mathematical constraints governing weak integrability breaking in qutrit quantum systems. It proves a cubic relationship between symmetry defects and current residuals, and shows that structural compensation can dramatically extend the time window for observing conserved energy-current correlations. The findings establish robust bounds on thermal memory even when the system is perturbed away from perfect integrability.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental limits on weak integrability breaking and the persistence of protected thermal memory in quantum systems near a qutrit exchange interaction.
main_result: It establishes a sharp cubic bound ($\delta^3 \le C\epsilon$) relating the symmetry defect to the current residual, and demonstrates that optimal compensation can extend the guaranteed energy-current correlation window to order $|\lambda|^{-3}$.
method: The analysis employs rigorous mathematical techniques involving Yang-Baxter deformations, commutator expansions, and the study of spectral measures in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The system is a qutrit chain undergoing exchange interactions, analyzed through the framework of Yang-Baxter deformations and weak perturbations ($\lambda$).
key_observables: Symmetry defect ($\delta$), local current-conservation residual ($\epsilon$), energy-current correlation window, and the eight-dimensional charge memory matrix.
important_parameters: Perturbation strength ($\lambda$), time scale ($t$), and the system size ($L$ in the thermodynamic limit).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of jointly analytic, regular Yang-Baxter deformations and that the thermodynamic limit is taken before the weak-coupling limit.
figures_summary: Figures compare the evolution of local residuals and initial current forces for raw versus optimally compensated paths, illustrating the improvement in scaling exponents.
paper_structure: The structure moves from establishing the fundamental symmetry constraints (Theorem 1) to deriving sharp quantitative bounds ($\delta^3 \le C\epsilon$), demonstrating the effect of structural compensation, and finally analyzing the resulting protected memory in the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: The work provides quantitative, rigorous bounds on how far a quantum system can be driven from integrability while retaining measurable, long-lived correlations, which is crucial for understanding thermalization dynamics.
